source_text: Cum adhuc, inquit, cum prosecutoribus essemus et me pater uerbis auertere et deicere pro sua affectione perseueraret: Pater, inquam, uides, uerbi gratia, uas hoc iacens, urceolum siue aliud? Et dixit: Video. Et ego dixi ei: Numquid alio nomine uocari potest quam quod est? Et ait: Non. Sic et ego aliud me dicere non possum nisi quod sum, Christiana. Tunc pater motus hoc uerbo mittit se in me, ut oculos mihi erueret; sed uexauit tantum, et profectus est uictus cum argumentis diaboli. Tunc paucis diebus quod caruissem patrem, domino gratias egi, et refrigeraui absentia illius. In ipso spatio paucorum dierum baptizati sumus; et mihi spiritus dictauit non aliud petendum ab aqua nisi sufferentiam carnis. Post paucos dies recipimur in carcerem: et expaui, quia numquam experta eram tales tenebras. O diem asperum! Aestus ualidus turbarum beneficio, concussurae militum. Nouissime macerabar sollicitudine infantis ibi. Tunc Tertius et Pomponius, benedicti diaconi qui nobis ministrabant, constituerunt praemio ut paucis horis emissi in meliorem locum carceris refrigeraremus. Tunc exeuntes de carcere uniuersi sibi uacabant: ego infantem lactabam iam inedia defectum; sollicita pro eo adloquebar matrem et confortabam fratrem, commendebam filium; tabescebam ideo quod illos tabescere uideram mei beneficio. Tales sollicitudines multis diebus passa sum, et usurpaui ut mecum infans in carcere maneret; et statim conualuit et releuata sum a labore et sollicitudine infantis, et factus est mihi carcer subito praetorium, ut ibi mallem essem quam alicubi.
pass_a_gloss: While we were still, she says, with the escorts and my father persisted in trying by words to turn me aside and pull me down out of his affection, I said: Father, do you see, for example, this vessel lying here, a small pitcher or something else? And he said: I see. And I said to him: Can it be called by another name than what it is? And he says: No. So also I am not able to call myself other than what I am, a Christian woman. Then my father, provoked by this word, rushes upon me as if to tear out my eyes; but he only maltreated me, and he departed beaten, with the devil's pleadings. Then because for a few days I had been without my father, I gave thanks to the Lord, and I took breath through his absence. In that interval of a few days we were baptized; and the Spirit put it into me to seek nothing from the water except endurance of the flesh. After a few days we are received into prison; and I was terrified, because I had never experienced such darkness. O harsh day! Violent heat by reason of the crowd, jostlings of the soldiers. Last of all I was worn thin by anxiety for the baby there. Then Tertius and Pomponius, the blessed deacons who were serving us, arranged by a payment that, let out for a few hours, we might get relief in a better part of the prison. Then as we came out of the prison, all attended to their own needs; I nursed my baby, already failing from hunger; being anxious for him, I spoke to my mother and I strengthened my brother and I entrusted my son; I was pining because I had seen them pine on my account. Such anxieties I suffered for many days, and I obtained that the baby should stay with me in prison; and at once he grew strong and I was lifted from toil and anxiety for the baby, and the prison suddenly became for me a headquarters, so that I would rather have been there than anywhere else.
pass_b_english: While we were still with our guards, she says, my father kept pleading with me in words, trying out of his love to turn me aside and bring me down. I said, Father, do you see this vessel lying here, for instance a little pitcher or something else. He said, I see. I said to him, Can it be called by any name other than what it is. He said, No. So I too cannot call myself anything other than what I am, a Christian. Then my father, stung by that word, flung himself at me as if to tear my eyes out, but he only hurt me, and he went away defeated, with the devil's arguments.

Then, because I was without my father for a few days, I gave thanks to the Lord, and I breathed again in his absence. In that stretch of a few days we were baptized, and the Spirit prompted me to seek nothing from the water except endurance in the flesh. A few days later we were taken into prison, and I was terrified, for I had never known such darkness. O harsh day. Fierce heat from the crowd, the shoving of the soldiers. And last of all I was worn thin with anxiety for my baby there. Then Tertius and Pomponius, the blessed deacons who were attending to us, arranged by a payment that we should be let out for a few hours into a better part of the prison and catch our breath.

Then, coming out of the prison, everyone attended to his own need, while I nursed my baby, who was already faint from hunger. Anxious for him, I spoke to my mother and I comforted my brother and I entrusted my son to them, and I pined away because I saw them pining away on my account. Such anxieties I endured for many days, and I obtained leave for the baby to remain with me in prison. At once he recovered his strength, and I was lifted from the burden and anxiety for my baby, and suddenly the prison became a palace for me, so that I would rather have been there than anywhere else.

lemmas.gloss: a Christian woman, what she is

choices.why: ablative of motive with affectione, and context is a father's pleading rather than legal affection; renders paternal feeling

choices.english: I breathed again in his absence / we might catch our breath
choices.why: refrigerare here is relief from pressure and heat, not doctrinal refreshment; the prison context and absentia require physical and mental breathing-space
cum is accompaniment and argumentis is ablative plural; father leaves as loser together with the diabolic pleadings that had worked through him
rejected: by the arguments of the devil alone

choices.term: factus est mihi carcer subito praetorium
choices.english: the prison suddenly became a headquarters-palace for me
choices.why: dative of advantage mihi plus predicative praetorium; sudden change of experience, not building change, so keeps both military and palatial sense
rejected: the prison was made a praetorium

variants: de carcere (Tunc exeuntes de carcere): forsitan additamentum F — kept as printed.
